subject: Post-call: throughput thresholds & recommended pilot plan
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.com>
To: Alex Kim <alex@brightretail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-30T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: throughput thresholds & recommended pilot plan

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery: your primary goal is to reduce latency on real-time product recommendations served to your mobile app while keeping per-request cost predictable as traffic grows. You walked us through the following numbers:~

- Peak write+read QPS for recommendation endpoint: ~1,200 QPS (spikes up to ~1,800 during promotions)
- 95th percentile latency target: <= 120ms end-to-end for the model inference portion
- Average request token length: ~45 tokens; max observed ~150 tokens
- Regional preference: us-east primary with eu-west as secondary for DR

Based on the call, we flagged two paths to evaluate: Hosted API (fast onboarding, simpler scaling) vs Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pools for predictable tail latency). To move the conversation forward I need two quick clarifications from your infra/product team:~

1) Can you confirm whether the 1,200 QPS is sustained or if it is bursty (e.g., sustained for minutes vs sustained for hours)?
2) What latency budget do you have for the network hop (client <-> service)? Is there an existing CDN or edge cache in front of the app calls?
3) Are there contractual constraints that would push you toward Dedicated or Private (e.g., data residency, SOC2 evidence already in place)?

Next steps I propose:~

- If you confirm bursts and strict tail SLAs, we recommend a 2-week Dedicated pilot with a small reserved pool to validate 95th%-tile latency at production mix.
- If traffic is more sustained and you prefer lower operational overhead, we can scope a Hosted API test with request shaping and KV-caching to hit latency targets.

Attached is the call recording and a preliminary throughput/SLA estimate we sketched during the call.

Can you loop in the person who owns the platform/networking so we can answer the CDN/network question quickly?

Thanks —
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[jasmine@redwood.com]

From: Alex Kim <alex@brightretail.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.com>
Cc: Platform Team <platform@brightretail.com>
Date: 2027-05-31T09:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: throughput thresholds & recommended pilot plan

Thanks, Jasmine — good summary. A couple answers inline:~

- The 1,200 QPS is sustained during business hours (roughly 10:00–18:00 PT) and we get the 1,800 QPS spikes for short windows (3–12 minutes) during flash promotions.
- Network hop: we have a CDN (FastEdge) terminating at our API gateway; typical network overhead to our service tier is ~20–30ms.
- Compliance: we have SOC2 in place but we still require an executed DPA and specific logging retention for audit trails. That leans us toward Dedicated or Private but not strictly required if Hosted API can provide the retention and KMS controls.

Two asks from our side:~

1) Rough ballpark: what kind of monthly committed spend would you expect for a Dedicated pool sized to handle 1.5k sustained QPS with the observed token distribution?
2) Timeline: if we go with the Dedicated pilot, how long until we can stand up a small pool and run our traffic?

If it helps, I can open a quick Confluence page with our traffic shapes — sending to platform@.

—Alex
Senior Engineering Manager, Bright Retail

- Compliance: Dedicated + customer-controlled KMS will satisfy their DPA/SOC2 asks; for Hosted, we'd need to map retention and KMS controls explicitly.

Action items:~
